intervals.label: magnet installation
intervals.quote: the 20-ton solenoid was installed as part of the sPHENIX assembly project in 2021

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: sPHENIX construction was completed in April 2023.

intervals.label: commissioning / first Au+Au data
intervals.quote: It was commissioned and took first Au+Au data in the RHIC 2023 Run.

intervals.label: physics operation
intervals.quote: For Run 25, the sPHENIX detector, which began operations in 2023, will be using all its capabilities for the first time to study the QGP produced in gold-gold collisions.

intervals.label: RHIC 25th and final run ends
intervals.locator: BNL Newsroom, "A Smashing Success: Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider Wraps up Final Collisions", 2026-02

total_mass.quote: The sPHENIX detector is about the size of a two-story house and weighs 1,000 tons.

subsystems.quote: A 20-ton cylindrical solenoid originally from the BaBar experiment at SLAC. It operates at 4 degrees Kelvin (-452 F)
subsystems.value: Superconducting solenoid magnet (reused from BaBar at SLAC), operating at 4 K

subsystems.quote: The electromagnetic calorimeter uses tungsten bricks with scintillating fibers to track electrons and photons.
subsystems.value: Electromagnetic calorimeter using tungsten bricks with embedded scintillating fibers

summary.plain: A new, house-sized particle detector at Brookhaven, built with a recycled magnet from the BaBar experiment, that records energetic jets and rare particles from nuclear collisions.
summary.technical: sPHENIX: a 1,000 t hermetic collider detector at RHIC IP8 built around a reused 20-ton BaBar solenoid (4 K) with tungsten-scintillating-fiber electromagnetic calorimetry; construction completed April 2023, commissioned with first Au+Au data in 2023.

technology.quote: A 20-ton cylindrical solenoid originally from the BaBar experiment at SLAC. It operates at 4 degrees Kelvin (-452 F) and bends charged particle trajectories to identify particle masses and interactions.
technology.value: Hermetic, solenoidal collider detector with electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry around a central tracking system, built inside a 20-ton reused BaBar solenoid magnet
